projectTitle: Glassica: Three prototypes of one hexagon puzzle
project_haiku: Glassica is a puzzle of rotating hexagonal rings and colors that mix when they overlap. We prototyped it as an iOS app, a two-player game in p5.js, and a laser-cut board.
project_footer_CTA: Need to find out if a game works before you commit to one platform? Glassica is three prototypes of the same rules.
pageSummary:
The job

The idea was a board of concentric hexagonal rings, polyiamond pieces, and colors that mix. It had to work as a solitaire puzzle and as a two-player contest. The way to learn that was to build it more than once.

What we built

The first prototype is an iOS puzzle. Pieces snap to the grid, rings rotate by a drag, and overlapping primary colors mix. A full hexagon of a complementary color clears and scores. The second is a two-player version in p5.js, to test territory rather than a solo clear. The third is a physical board, cut by laser, so the same rotation could be tried with hands.

The technology line on this project is C# and Unity, which is where the native prototype work sat alongside the p5.js and the physical board.

Outcomes

The rules survived contact with a screen and with a table. That is what the prototypes were for.
